chunks: "You cast it first," answered Moses. When they cast their spell, they bewitched the eyes of the people and petrified them by conjuring up a great charm.
ai.seo_question: How did Pharaoh's magicians affect the people's perception during the confrontation with Moses?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse highlights the psychological warfare employed by Pharaoh's court, where the magicians' illusion was not merely visual but deeply rooted in instilling terror (istirhab) to validate Pharaoh's divine claim. The 'great magic' (sihr 'azim) refers to the widespread perception of the phenomenon, which temporarily overshadowed the people's faith until Moses' staff consumed their illusions, demonstrating the superiority of divine truth over ephemeral power.
